children: shares have dropped nearly 10% over the past week, but the brokerage's latest August operating data shows that customer growth, trading activity and platform assets remain strong enough to keep the investment case alive. The key question for investors is whether that operating momentum can continue translating into durable earnings as the stock trades at an elevated valuation.

Robinhood operates a retail investing platform offering commission-free stock and options trading, cryptocurrency trading, margin lending and other financial services. Its revenue is driven by transaction activity, interest income, subscriptions and other platform-based services.

The company ended August with 28.6 million funded customers, up roughly 120,000 from July and 1.9 million from a year earlier. Total platform assets climbed 8% month over month to $383.7 billion, while net deposits reached $4 billion.
Platform growth remains the key story.
Trading activity also remained strong. Equity trading volume jumped 68% from a year earlier to $335.4 billion, while options contracts increased 50% to 292.5 million.
Event contracts continued to expand rapidly, reaching 4.7 billion, roughly 15 times the year-earlier level.

Crypto activity rebounded sharply from July. Total crypto trading volume increased 61% sequentially to $17.5 billion, although it remained 38% below August 2025. Robinhood app crypto volume climbed 72% month over month to $7.4 billion, while Bitstamp generated $10.1 billion, up 53%.
Margin balances also rose 72% year over year to $21.5 billion, potentially supporting higher interest income.
The most important metrics are funded-customer growth, net deposits, platform assets and whether elevated trading activity remains sustainable.

Robinhood shares were trading around $112.81 despite the recent weekly decline, but the stock has still gained 25.45% since Aug. 1, sharply outperforming the S&P 500's 0.11% decline over the same period.

That performance raises the hurdle for future results. Continued growth in margin balances, options, event contracts and customer assets could support earnings expansion. A slowdown in deposits or trading volumes, however, would make Robinhood's elevated valuation harder to defend.

title: Robinhood Stock Pullback May Be Misleading
